acceptance: Given a paired row whose `auth_type` the source shows differently from the sheet, the output row is `corrected`, with `auth_type`, `proposed_access`, `permissions_to_confirm` and `unknowns` following the rules for that type, and no permission or scope is invented; and a row whose `auth_type` is free text ends with one of `website-sign-in`, `api-credential`, `other` or `unknown` (mapped only where the text unambiguously names one kind, otherwise `unknown`), is `corrected`, and has its original wording listed in the report. (B01)

Given an unpaired finding, the `new` row has `auth_type`, `proposed_access`, `permissions_to_confirm` and `unknowns` filled by the rules (including `reuse of an existing CI identity: unconfirmed`) and `use_case_ref` filled, with every other human-owned and forbidden column blank. (B03)
Given human-owned or forbidden cells outside their allowed list or format, the cells are copied exactly as typed and the report lists each by row and column. (B05)

Given a document-only row, an identity name and a CI identity, the output keeps a `not in source` row byte-equal, writes `identity_reference` as `NAME (runtime value unknown)`, drops the document-only prefix only when a `source:` pointer is added and the source shows the observed access, and the checklist's drift section lists every restated rule, including the allowed `auth_type` values and the spec text shapes, with the sibling section it matches, the examples having been compared with the sample workbook. (B06, B07, B10)
